patterns.name: Two Pointers
patterns.description: Use two indices moving toward/away from each other to reduce O(n²) to O(n).

patterns.name: Sliding Window
patterns.description: Maintain a window of elements; expand/shrink to satisfy a constraint.

patterns.name: Prefix Sum / Difference Array
patterns.description: Precompute cumulative sums for O(1) range queries.

patterns.name: Kadane's / Greedy on Arrays
patterns.description: Track local and global maximum for maximum subarray problems.

patterns.name: Sorting & Searching in Arrays
patterns.description: Sort once, then binary-search for O(n log n) solutions.

patterns.name: String Manipulation & Hashing
patterns.description: Count character frequencies to compare or find patterns.

patterns.name: Sliding Window on Strings
patterns.description: Track character counts inside a variable-size window.

patterns.name: Pattern Matching
patterns.description: KMP / Rabin-Karp / Z-Algorithm for efficient O(n+m) substring search.

patterns.name: Stack-based String Problems
patterns.description: Process characters left-to-right with a monotonic or explicit stack.

patterns.name: Fast & Slow Pointers
patterns.description: Floyd's Cycle Detection — two pointers at different speeds to detect cycles and midpoints.

patterns.name: Reversal & Merging
patterns.description: Reverse sublists or entire lists using pointer manipulation.

patterns.name: Advanced Linked List
patterns.description: Complex linked list operations including arithmetic, deduplication, and design.

patterns.name: Monotonic Stack
patterns.description: Maintain a stack in increasing/decreasing order for next-greater/smaller queries.

patterns.name: Queue / Deque Patterns
patterns.description: Maintain a deque for sliding window max/min in O(n).

patterns.name: Classic Binary Search
patterns.description: Repeatedly halve the search space on a monotonic function.

patterns.name: Binary Search on Answer
patterns.description: Binary search on the answer space, validate with a feasibility function.

patterns.name: Bisect Tricks
patterns.description: Advanced binary search applications like LIS in O(n log n).

patterns.name: Tree Traversals
patterns.description: DFS (Pre/In/Post-order) & BFS (Level-order) — foundation of nearly all tree problems.

patterns.name: Binary Tree Properties
patterns.description: Solve sub-problems on left/right subtrees and combine results via recursion.

patterns.name: Binary Search Trees (BST)
patterns.description: BST Property — left < root < right; enables O(log n) search, insert, delete.

patterns.name: Tries
patterns.description: Trie (Prefix Tree) for efficient prefix search and autocomplete in O(L) per query.

patterns.name: Top-K Pattern
patterns.description: Min-Heap of size K to maintain the K largest elements efficiently.

patterns.name: Two-Heap Pattern
patterns.description: One max-heap and one min-heap to find the median dynamically.

patterns.name: BFS (Shortest Path / Level-order)
patterns.description: Explore nodes level by level; guarantees shortest path in unweighted graphs.

patterns.name: DFS / Backtracking on Graphs
patterns.description: Explore all paths; detect cycles and connected components.

patterns.name: Topological Sort
patterns.description: Kahn's Algorithm / DFS Post-order for linear ordering of nodes in a DAG.

patterns.name: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
patterns.description: DSU with Path Compression + Union by Rank for near-O(1) amortised operations.

patterns.name: Shortest Path Algorithms
patterns.description: Dijkstra / Bellman-Ford / Floyd-Warshall for weighted shortest paths.

patterns.name: Minimum Spanning Tree
patterns.description: Kruskal's / Prim's — greedily build a spanning tree with minimum total edge weight.

patterns.name: 1-D DP (Linear Recurrences)
patterns.description: State is a single index; transition from previous states.

patterns.name: 2-D DP (Grid / Two Sequences)
patterns.description: State is two indices (i, j); fill a table row by row.

patterns.name: Knapsack Variants
patterns.description: 0/1 Knapsack / Unbounded Knapsack — classic DP on items with weight/value.

patterns.name: Interval / Range DP
patterns.description: Solve subproblems over all intervals [i, j], merge results.

patterns.name: Bitmask DP
patterns.description: Represent subsets as bitmasks; ideal for small n (≤20).

patterns.name: DP on Trees & Graphs
patterns.description: Dynamic programming applied to tree and graph structures.

patterns.name: Subsets & Combinations
patterns.description: Explore all choices recursively; prune branches that violate constraints.

patterns.name: Permutations
patterns.description: Swap elements or use a visited array for permutation generation.

patterns.name: Advanced Backtracking
patterns.description: Complex backtracking with string splitting, tiling, and constraint satisfaction.

patterns.name: Interval & Scheduling Greedy
patterns.description: Always pick the locally optimal choice; prove exchange argument.

patterns.name: String & Array Greedy
patterns.description: Greedy approaches for string manipulation and array optimization.

patterns.name: HashMap / HashSet Patterns
patterns.description: O(1) lookups to avoid nested loops; track frequency, index, or pairs.

patterns.name: Math & Number Theory
patterns.description: Prime sieves, GCD/LCM, modular arithmetic, combinatorics.

patterns.name: Bit Manipulation
patterns.description: XOR, AND/OR masks, Brian Kernighan's algorithm for O(1) bit operations.

patterns.name: Classic Design Problems
patterns.description: OOP + Right Data Structures — combine hash maps, heaps, doubly linked lists for O(1) ops.

patterns.name: Randomized & Probabilistic Structures
patterns.description: Reservoir Sampling / Fisher-Yates for uniform random sampling in O(1) space.

patterns.name: Stream / Online Algorithms
patterns.description: Process data one element at a time without looking back.

patterns.name: Advanced Design Challenges
patterns.description: Complex data structure design combining multiple techniques.
